review_notes:
I read the whole file and looked for nontrivial reasoning that appears in two or more proofs. I found nothing that meets the rubric's bar. I did not open any other source files and I did not check for duplicates elsewhere in the library. The closest candidates were all short:
- `Iso.mapEdgeSet`: the `left_inv` and `right_inv` blocks are the same four-line script. One is the other applied to `f.symm`, so a helper would save only a few lines.
- `Embedding.map_mem_edgeSet_iff` and `Iso.map_mem_edgeSet_iff`: each is the one-liner `Sym2.ind (fun _ _ => f.map_adj_iff) e`. This is a thin wrapper, not repeated machinery.
- `Embedding.mapNeighborSet` and `Iso.mapNeighborSet`: both build `⟨f w, f.apply_mem_neighborSet_iff.mpr w.2⟩`. This is routine construction.
- `map_le_of_le_comap` and `map_monotone`: both use `rintro` on the `Relation.Map` witnesses, but this is routine unfolding.
- `Iso.symm_toHom_comp_toHom` and `Iso.toHom_comp_symm_toHom`: both are simp-only calls with different lemmas, so they are trivial.
I found no hidden degenerate-case issues.
